title: Man shot by police had replica handgun: Daniel Anthony King shot at Mohawk gas station after leading cops on a wild chase in stolen car
article: The handgun pulled out by a man shot dead by police in Burnaby early Friday morning was a replica, the RCMP revealed Monday.
Pitt Meadows resident Daniel Antony King, 37, was shot at 12:23 a.m. at the Mohawk Gas Station at the corner of Canada Way and Edmonds after leading police on a wild chase in a stolen car.
Police initially told reporters that King produced a handgun before he was shot.

But in a news release sent out just before 5 p.m. Monday, the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team -- which is investigating the shooting -- said forensic specialists have confirmed the weapon was actually an imitation handgun.
No photo of the replica gun was released, but police have said in the past that replica handguns can often look almost identical to real firearms.

According to the news release, the incident began just after midnight, when a Coquitlam RCMP officer tried to pull over a vehicle whose occupants were acting suspiciously near Lougheed Highway and Barnet Highway.
As the officer tried to pull the vehicle over, it sped off into the oncoming lanes of Lougheed Highway -- and the officer abandoned the chase.
A check of the licence plate number revealed the vehicle was stolen.
The RCMP helicopter was called to the area and followed the vehicle as it fled toward Highway 1 in a "very dangerous manner", according to the release.
A second attempt was made to stop the car, but it then began heading westbound into oncoming traffic on Highway 1.
The vehicle continued to be observed from the air as it moved into the proper lane and headed towards Vancouver.
The helicopter then observed the vehicle entering the Mohawk gas station and four police vehicles from both Burnaby and New Westminster arrived at the scene.
According to police, as the officers tried to box the suspect in, he attempted to ram the car into the police cruisers in an attempt to escape.
Four officers approached the vehicle on foot and, according to the release, when the officers reached the driver's door, "the driver was observed to produce a handgun."
As a result, two officers shot King several times.
King was rushed to Royal Columbian Hospital where he was pronounced dead.
His female passenger, who was not injured, was arrested for possession of stolen property. She has since been released pending trial.
Police say that the vehicle in question was reported stolen from Vancouver on Oct. 5 and that it also had stolen plates.
According to the news release, King was "known to police".
Police provided no details on King's criminal past.

But, according to a Vancouver police news release, a Daniel King, 37, rammed a stolen car into a police cruiser in Vancouver on April 10, 2005, after the officer parked in front of his vehicle to try to stop him from leaving.
And on Jan. 27, 2005, according to Vancouver police, King held a gun to his head for three hours -- keeping police at bay -- after an officer found him sleeping in a parked stolen car.
